title: Ptolemy's world, measured
excerpt: Ptolemy wrote the ancient world down as a table of coordinates. I matched 2,358 of his places to where they really are: shrink his longitudes by 0.72 and the map falls into place, but Scotland is still turned on its side and Sri Lanka is 15 times too big.
seo_description: Ptolemy's Geography (about AD 150) set against a modern map: 2,358 places, the stretch in longitude, Scotland, India and Taprobane.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Ptolemy's World' in black and red on pale paper, beside a grid of Ptolemy's degrees dotted with thousands of coloured places and brown coastlines, and a small modern map with his coasts shrunk to fit. Text: 2,358 places, longitudes times 0.72, Sri Lanka 15 times too big.
